tasks.short: Respond to public inquiries and complaints about a site plan

steps.what: Read public inquiries and note site, ask and sender
Open the plan file those inquiries name
Draft replies to the public inquiries from that plan

loop.input: her inquiry note and the plan extract she opened
loop.output: a reply draft that answers the written ask
loop.check: the reply answers the ask she wrote, and each cited rule is a sentence in the plan she opened, not only a file number
loop.stop: she accepts the draft or rewrites it herself after one pass
loop.why_not_simpler: a fixed template cannot match a free-text inquiry to the right sentence in the plan

steps.what: Check the reply answers those inquiries and the plan
Send the accepted reply on those public inquiries
Meet people about complaints a mail reply cannot close

tasks.design: She writes the site, the ask and the sender from each public inquiry, then opens the plan in the {DOCS} store. A bounded loop drafts a reply from that plan into {EMAIL}; she checks that it answers her ask and that each cited rule is a sentence in the file she opened. Only that accepted reply is sent. Any later edit voids the acceptance. Complaints that need a meeting stay with her, and she keeps the reply headings herself.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each inquiry is free text tied to a local plan, and a sentence sent to the public can be read as the company's position.
tasks.enabler_now: A short loop can draft from a plan she has already opened, and the mailbox can send only a version she has accepted.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing which plan applies, and a complaint that needs a meeting, stay with her. A sentence that is really in the file can still be the wrong reading of the rule.
tasks.human_edge: She decides what the company will tell the public, and she meets people whose complaint a mail cannot close.

ambition.what: The day she names the plan, she decides whether a written inquiry is a routine reply or a meeting.

tasks.altitude: Routine written replies take less of the week. She still signs every reply that goes out, and complaint meetings stay on her calendar.

reach.task: Answer a written question about access to the same site
reach.learn: Cite the plan file the urban planner already opened, and send nothing until that planner has accepted the reply.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge (E1): the digest's planning note says zoning rules can be configuration and that a model may pre-read a report a planner then signs. No source in the digest shows a product that answers public planning inquiries. This design only drafts from the plan she opened.
AI Act article 50 requires disclosure of AI text that informs the public unless a human is the editor. She edits and accepts every reply before it is sent, so the outgoing text is hers.
Deloitte partly refunded an A$440,000 government report that contained fabricated references. That is why each cited plan sentence must appear in the file she opened before a reply is sent.

assumptions: The focal person is the company's urban planner. She answers residents and applicants about sites the company is planning. The workflow boundary is the written reply plus the complaint meeting; she does not grant permits.

Before a draft, she records three fields on the inquiry note: site, ask, and sender. She is the producer. If the mail is messy she types them. There is no separate permit system; the plan file is already in the {DOCS} store.
She already emails replies today, so the send is a real step. Opening the plan stays her time. Store and mailbox runtime is not her hours.
Reply headings and the list of plan fields a draft may cite are her upkeep, not a machine step.
In this company more inquiries arrive by mail than at a counter, so the meeting share is below the occupation prior and covers only complaints a written reply cannot close.
unknowns: Whether national works-council rules require consent before a draft tool reads her mailbox.
Which plan file is authoritative when two versions exist.
What share of this company's inquiries are visits rather than mail.
research_questions: What share of her week is written inquiries versus complaint meetings?
Who else is allowed to send a public reply today?

already_counted.description: She still checks every reply against the ask and the plan she opened.
She still meets on complaints a written reply cannot close.

incremental.description: She keeps the reply headings and the list of plan fields a draft may cite.

approvals.approved_version: accepted reply the urban planner released

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a week of counter complaints, so the mail draft barely runs. High: a week of written inquiries where she has already named the plan file. Both sit under the net after she keeps the reply headings.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: She still owns what the company tells the public. Routine written replies take less of the week; complaint meetings and the choice of plan stay hers.
skills_to_grow: Tell a routine written inquiry from a complaint that needs a meeting
Match each cited sentence to the plan she opened before a reply goes out
role.ambitious_version: A draft waits the same day she names the plan, and she still signs every reply that leaves. No reply goes out unedited, and no complaint meeting is replaced by mail.
